title: Michael S NDE 3137
content: Well when I was seven years old I had been rocking on a chair in the kitchen. I lost balance when I was rocking the chair and hit the back of my skull on the corner of the handle. My mom said she thought I was joking at first because she saw me shaking and stuck to the handle. She realized I had hit my head when she pulled me forward - I fell on the ground and blood started hitting the ceiling. I remember my mom driving and my grandma holding me in between her legs, with me bent over with a cloth over my head. They were following an ambulance, which they had called. Until this, I remember the part where I was above the car, which we were driving, a brown two-door convertible. Then I had just woken up while they were wrapping the bandage over the stitches or staples. The funny thing is I remember the time I was above the brown two-door car convertible, but don't remember the time I was recovering from the injury. The second time was when I was nine years old I had a tonsil surgery and I had an allergic reaction to the anesthesia. After waking up from the surgery, I felt paralyzed. I could not open my eyes or even speak. I was just lying there listening to the doctor say to me what had happened. I was so scared I yelled inside my head and moved as hard as I could. I went straight into the air, far away it felt, but I couldn't see or hear anything; only it was all clusters of white and black in front of me. All of a sudden, I had a feeling as though I was shot straight back down even faster than I went up. I was over my body looking down from the corner of the room from the left side of the body. I was in the middle of a really big room with my father next to me sitting on the chair. I saw he had a un-wrapped present in his hands which was a 'Wilson' basketball, that was what I wanted for a long time as a kid, it was my first basketball. I remember waking up and asking the people around me the first thing, 'Where is my basketball?' Everyone was surprised on how I knew about the ball. They asked the doctor. He replied that I had overheard everything. Then I replied, 'Where is the 'Wilson' basketball?' Then they were even more shocked when they learned that my father had only told me that he had bought me a new basketball and had never mentioned the brand 'Wilson'.

out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: He felt scared, 'yelled inside my head,' went 'straight into the air,' then felt 'shot straight back down.'

environment.environment_other_detail: He reported seeing 'clusters of white and black' and later described being in 'a really big room.'

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Age 7: fell while rocking a chair and hit the back of his skull on a handle corner; heavy bleeding. Age 9: tonsil surgery with allergic reaction to anesthesia and paralysis.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Two episodes: (1) age 7 OBE above the car while being driven after head injury; (2) age 9 anesthesia reaction with upward movement into 'clusters of white and black,' then rapid return and OBE from room corner observing father and a 'Wilson' basketball.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Second episode: paralysis in bed → felt going up (no seeing/hearing; black/white clusters) → shot back down → OBE from room corner looking at body and room → woke in body.
stage_sequence.repeated_stage_detail: OBE occurred in both events (age 7 above car; age 9 room-corner view over body).

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Reported inability to see/hear while 'straight into the air' with only 'clusters of white and black' visible before being 'shot straight back down.'
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “I remember the part where I was above the car… a brown two-door convertible.” “I could not open my eyes or even speak.” “I went straight into the air… but I couldn't see or hear anything; only it was all clusters of white and black in front of me.” “I had a feeling as though I was shot straight back down…” “Where is the 'Wilson' basketball?”
